newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty soars vs basket, seen bullish.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty soars vs basket, seen bullish.

text.p: The zloty, boosted by foreign investor entry into Polish fixed bonds, firmed against the basket of currencies and broke through resistance levels without triggering a central bank currency-buying intervenion.
Dealers said the zloty might remain bullish on Thursday and head toward three percent from the trading band centre as more foreign investors had to purchase zlotys for fixed bonds.
"Today's currency selling was largely due to expectations of large-scale foreign entry in bonds, and this mood may continue tomorrow," said Tomasz Nowakowski of Bank Handlowy SA.
The zloty closed at 2.80/2.71 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Tuesday's 2.54/2.48 percent.
It opened at 3.0040/60 to the dollar, down from 3.0025/40 on Tuesday and at 1.8185/05 to the mark, up from 1.8285/95.

Dealers said foreign investors bought most of the 552 million zlotys of 12-percent five-year bonds sold at today's tender and that the majority still had not done forex transactions. The value date for the auction is February 12.
On Wednesday the zloty broke through a barrier at 2.5 percent from the parity rate and dealers said 3.0 percent from parity was likely to be its next key resistance level.
Dealers said mainly large foreign funds and longer-term investors were interested in Poland's five-year bonds.
"For the longer term it's a good buy for foreigners at 18.5 percent per year," said Piotr Bednarek of ING Bank in Warsaw.
Poland also sold 146 million zlotys of 15-percent two-year bonds, which gave a yield of around 20.65 percent.

The money market regained liquidity after banks payed for treasury operations on Wednesday. Overnight rates closed at 21.90/22.50 percent, down from opening's 23.40/23.65 and tomorrow/next at 21.90/22.30 from 23.45/24.00.
